title: Evaluation of a common prescribing cascade of calcium channel blockers and diuretics in older adults with hypertension
authors: Savage RD, Visentin JD, Bronskill SE, Wang X, Gruneir A, Giannakeas V, et al.
followUp: 90 days, with analyses up to 1 year
population: Community-dwelling adults aged 66 or older with hypertension in Ontario, Canada, with new prescription claims from 30 September 2011 to 30 September 2016: 41,086 newly dispensed a calcium channel blocker, 66,494 an ACE inhibitor or angiotensin receptor blocker and 231,439 an unrelated drug; mean age 74.5 years, 56.5% women
funder: This research was supported by project grant PJT-153060 from the Canadian Institutes of Health Research. This study was supported by ICES, which is funded by an annual grant from the Ontario Ministry of Health and Long-Term Care. The funding sources had no role in the design and conduct of the study; collection, management, analysis, and interpretation of the data; preparation, review, or approval of the manuscript; and decision to submit the manuscript for publication.
inKindSupport: IMS Brogan Inc provided use of its Drug Information Database.
result: Cumulative incidence of a loop diuretic dispensed within 90 days: 1.4% after a new calcium channel blocker against 0.7% after a new ACE inhibitor or angiotensin receptor blocker and 0.5% after an unrelated drug (P<0.001). Adjusted hazard ratios against ACE inhibitor or receptor blocker: 1.68 (95% CI 1.38 to 2.05) for days 1 to 30, 2.26 (1.76 to 2.92) for days 31 to 60 and 2.40 (1.84 to 3.13) for days 61 to 90; against unrelated drugs 2.51, 2.99 and 3.89. The association persisted, slightly attenuated, up to 1 year and in the subgroup newly dispensed amlodipine. The authors describe the cascade as oedema misinterpreted as a new condition and treated with a diuretic.
